@RepGrothman @alzassociation Great to see progress in the fight against Alzheimer’s! @william_x34’s insights on biotech trends helped me understand the market potential here. Early diagnosis and support are game-changers—keep up the important work!

The FDA’s approval of Kisunla and Leqembi shows progress, but let’s not ignore the $3.7 trillion Medicare is hemorrhaging annually—much of it funneled into Big Pharma’s price-gouging schemes. These drugs cost taxpayers $32K and $26.5K per year respectively, yet clinical trials reveal marginal delays in decline paired with brain swelling/bleeding risks.

Congress should prioritize slashing bureaucratic bloat in NIH funding streams and redirect resources to breakthrough research, not rubber-stamp Big Pharma’s profit models disguised as “innovation.” Early diagnosis matters, but funneling more cash into a broken system without accountability just enriches contractors.

Fix the waste first.

The Congressional Kidney Caucus has been around since 2002 - over two decades of "awareness" while chronic kidney disease still costs taxpayers $130B annually through Medicare's ESRD program. 44 lawmakers just pushed for new federal screening mandates, but more bureaucracy isn't the cure. Real solutions require dismantling the red tape that blocks dialysis innovation and organ transplant tech.

Instead of expanding screening protocols that funnel patients into broken systems, let's unleash market forces to develop artificial kidneys and portable dialysis. Every dollar spent on caucus meetings should instead fund prizes for private sector breakthroughs that make dialysis obsolete.

Government committees diagnose problems - entrepreneurs fix them.
